metaDescription: Smooth Cayenne pineapple is an introduced pineapple variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Smooth Cayenne pineapple is an introduced pineapple variety, also sold or known as Cayenne or Hawaiian pineapple. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from introduced cultivar.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Smooth Cayenne pineapple is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Cayenne or Hawaiian pineapple, this is the same pineapple. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [pineapple variety finder](/crop-varieties/pineapple), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Smooth Cayenne pineapple

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pineapple fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Cylindrical, 2.5 to 3 kg, pale yellow to yellow flesh, high in sugar and acid.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: introduced by the American era Bureau of Agriculture in the early 1900s, its sweet, acidic fruit suits canning. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Smooth Cayenne pineapple

Queen types such as Formosa are small and sweet, and Smooth Cayenne is big and juicy for processing. Plant suckers or slips of one type so the field ripens together. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Cayenne the same as Smooth Cayenne?
items.a: Yes. Cayenne is another name for Smooth Cayenne. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Smooth Cayenne?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
